key_insight: Lexicographically minimizing idle range, maximum idle, then total idle can reduce waiting while preserving optimal balance in B2B meeting schedules.
engineering_relevance: Compact MaxSAT encodings offer a lower-memory approach to balanced meeting scheduling, though fewer clauses do not consistently imply faster solving.
method: Measure waiting as empty slots between each participant’s first and last meetings.
Optimize idle range, maximum idle, and total idle in strict priority order.
Compare Direct, Compact-Base, and Compact-Objective encodings with proven preservation of feasibility, costs, and priorities.
evidence_signal: Tests covered 226 variants of 20 base instances with three repetitions per configuration; among 84 instances optimal under all three quality objectives, selected lexicographic schedules preserved optimal range and reduced maximum idle on 11 and total idle on 56 versus selected range-only schedules.
watch_item: Runtime rankings varied, so benchmark the encodings on target workloads rather than treating clause reductions as guaranteed speedups.
paper_title: Compact MaxSAT Encodings for Balanced Waiting in B2B Meeting Scheduling
